concepts.learning_objective: Identify the limitations of manual record keeping and the benefits of storing records in computer files.
Describe a file as a container of data and explain that application programs are needed to access file data.
Explain data redundancy and how it leads to data inconsistency in a file system.
Explain data isolation and data dependence as limitations of a file system.
Explain the difficulty of access and of controlled data sharing in a file system.
Define a DBMS, give examples and state what querying a database means.
Explain how related files are redesigned into tables of a database to remove redundancy.
State the costs and limitations of moving from a file system to a DBMS.
Distinguish a database schema from a database instance.
Explain data constraints and meta-data stored in the database catalog.
Identify queries and the insertion, deletion and update operations on a database.
Identify the relational data model among the types of data models.
Define relation, attribute, tuple and domain in the relational data model.
Find the degree and cardinality of a relation.

topics.title: Three Important Properties of a Relation

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the rules on attribute names, distinct tuples and the order of tuples and attributes.
Apply the rules on domains, atomic values and the use of NULL in a relation.
Identify candidate, primary and alternate keys of a relation.
Explain when a composite primary key is needed and identify one.
Explain how a foreign key relates two relations and restricts the values that can be stored.
